document.abstract: A cathode-ray tube with a screen consisting of three phosphor bands fluorescing in the primary colors of red, blue and green may, in principle, be used to effect wholly electronic reproduction of television pictures in natural color if field- or line-sequential transmitting norms are employed. However, this tube inherently suffers from two limitations: the screen area is inefficiently utilized from the standpoint of light output, and the resolution capabilities are inadequate.
